SWEEP A -- t25_falsifier_freshness. AT HEAD IT PRINTS 15 CROSS-LANE ROWS, NOT THE 14 THE ORDER NAMES: `CITED rows (high confidence) : 37 = 15 CROSS-LANE + 22 same-lane`, over `law records scanned : 793` and `attempt records scanned : 1426`. The order's count was stale before the lane started (the newest row, WS/CritterDamagePlayer, is stamped 2026-09-04T14:58:18Z, after the 14:44:12Z record the order was written from). DISPOSITIONS, all 15: (1) GENUINE, AND CLOSED THIS RUN -- AL_the-addr16lo-surplus-copy-roster v1 / CR ProcessCritterList: the attempt already carries `refutes` on the law, and this lane's commit c11ef24bc adds the `supersedes` edge via AL ...v2. (2) GENUINE CANDIDATE, NOT CLOSED, QUEUED FOR RUN 57 -- claim.law.PC_a-named-pointer-local-selects-the-displacement-load-and-its-declaration-site-decides-the-hoist.20260902.v1 / do_players: the newer DP record says the law is 'already refuted on its declaration-site clause by the superseded record's B/C pair', and an inbound `refutes` from attempt.PC_do-players-linkage-axis-closed-from-step0-artifact-and-the-assignment-site-decides.20260903.v1 exists, but the law carries `superseded_by: None`, so `laws` still ranks its title clause as settled. THIS RECORD DOES NOT AUTHOR THAT SUPERSESSION and states why: the law's BODY already records the conflict its title over-claims ('the twin sites are closed rather than solved', and its own falsifier names probes C and D as 'the recorded negatives for the two obvious declaration sites'), so whether the title over-claims relative to the body is a judgement that needs the do_players lane's context, not a custodial guess. Candidate, not bug. (3)-(15) THIRTEEN BENIGN: compliance citations, no edge owed, enumerated in counted_negatives. THE TRANSFERABLE FINDING: the sweep's CITED tier has no verb discriminator, so it hands a custodial lane 15 rows of which 2 matter -- an 87% benign rate on its highest-confidence tier. The discriminator is cheap and textual (SCREENED/APPLIED/HONOURED/CONFIRMED/NOT-applicable next to the law id = compliance; 'refuted'/'wrong'/'does not hold'/'counter-example' = contradiction) and belongs in the tool, which is a T26 item, not a defect in any record.

SWEEP B -- t25_record_recheck. THE SHIPPED TOOL HAS NO CORPUS MODE: `--help` takes one positional `record`, so its docstring's headline calibration ('8 read STALE', measured 030385209, in-process over the whole corpus) is not reproducible from any shipped entry point. Reproducing it required a driver over the module's advertised IMPORTABLE CORE. AT HEAD THE CORPUS READS 121 STALE, NOT 8: `records_total 2276, quote_metric 1595, quote_command 606, recheckable 546, ambiguous_multi_function 29, no_live_measurement 12, held 384, stale 121`, over 303 distinct (unit,function) pairs measured in 130s. Every bucket differs from the docstring's (355 attributable, 347 HELD, 8 STALE, 18 multi-function, 162 non-measuring), so the driver is NOT a faithful clone of that sweep and this record does not claim it is. WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH, because it is the part that can be checked against the shipped code: the COMPARISON is faithful. Three flagged rows re-run through the shipped CLI reproduce the driver's verdict exactly -- attempt.AL_movelogic22... `MOVED real: record [95, 72] -> live 0` with `HELD insns`, claim.law.PC_a-named-pointer-local... `MOVED real: record [1129] -> live 836`, evidence.playermotion-match-state.20260829.v1 `MOVED insns: record [(4775, 4776)] -> live (4775, 4767)`, each ending `VERDICT: STALE`. So the divergence from 8 lives in the SWEEP's attribution rules, not in the metric comparison, and the honest statement is that the docstring's figure cannot be confirmed or refuted from a shipped command. DISPOSITION OF THE 121, split two-sided rather than listed: 85 are ANCHORED (a commit-like token appears in the record, satisfying the tool's own alternative remedy) and 36 are UNANCHORED -- a moved number with no commit anywhere in the record, which is the actionable hazard set. By kind: 95 attempt, 24 claim, 2 evidence. Six of the 36 are one family, `attempt.mp-label-correction.*`, whose `insns` pairs have all moved (cardThreadMain [[133,130]]->[133,133], do_players [[1174,1160]]->[1174,1172], HealthMeterStart [[113,115]]->[113,113], HealthMeterUpdate [[231,230]]->[231,231], MBWorldToScreen3D [[104,102]]->[104,104], do_player_select [[1885,1885]]->[1885,1886]). A further subset now measures real 0 because the function CLOSED (PlayerDoWeapTrail in two records, CritterGetTargetPlayers, do_heal_players, init_game_cam, load_player_geo, damage_enemy), which is a record describing a win, not a defect. CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE EXISTING HYGIENE SCREEN, and the two are largely COMPLEMENTARY: `gdlmem stale` returns stale_solved 16, reopen_candidates 34, postprocessor_walls 114, and against this sweep's 76 distinct STALE functions the intersections are 2, 8 and 11 respectively. So t25_record_recheck is not duplicating `stale` -- `stale` asks whether a PARK is moot, t25 asks whether a QUOTED NUMBER still reproduces, and 65 of the 76 functions are seen by neither of stale's first two buckets. A FIRST-ATTEMPT MEASUREMENT OF THAT OVERLAP WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: keying the intersection on `record_id` returned 0 for all three buckets, because those rows carry keys `['function','fuzzy','record']` / `['function','missing_anchors','reason','record']` and no `record_id` at all, so every id read None and the empty intersection was an extraction artifact that reads exactly like a finding. Re-keyed on `function`, the real numbers are the ones above.

For the sweep-A claim: `python tools/gdl/composed_census/t25_falsifier_freshness.py` and read the citing record of any row this record calls benign -- if any of the thirteen turns out to contradict its law rather than comply with it, that row's edge IS owed and this disposition is wrong on that row. hypothesis.statement: BOTH SWEEPS NEED A SEVERITY COLUMN BEFORE A CUSTODIAL LANE CAN CONSUME THEM, AND IN BOTH CASES THE COLUMN IS CHEAP AND TEXTUAL. t25_falsifier_freshness should classify each CITED row by the VERB adjacent to the law id in the citing record (SCREENED/APPLIED/HONOURED/CONFIRMED/'NOT applicable' = compliance, no edge owed; 'refuted'/'wrong'/'does not hold'/'counter-example'/'tautology' = contradiction, edge owed) and print the two tiers separately -- measured here, that would have taken its highest-confidence tier from 15 rows to 2. t25_record_recheck should (a) ship a `--corpus` mode, since its own headline calibration is unreachable from its CLI, and (b) split STALE by whether the record anchors any number to a commit, which here is 85 against 36. Both are T26 items; neither is a defect in any record.
